Representation principle
Part–whole models establish whole/part structure. The rectangular form can bridge deliberately into proportional bar models: later, bar length begins to carry magnitude as well as relationship.

  • v35: applied the classroom interaction standard to all 12 then-current interactive tools; all now use Teach / Explore / Challenge, Freeze, Hide/Reveal, New Example and Full Screen controls, with broader objective-specific presets.

  • v33: added Interactive Maths Tools view, objective-aware tool links and refined v2 tool bank.
  • v32: final word-boundary cleanup in diagnostic matching (including centimetres/time and rectangle/angle false positives).
  • v31: diagnostic probes diversified at objective level; inappropriate cross-topic reused probes removed; final stabilisation checks.
  • v30: stabilisation audit; consolidated type overrides; shared diagnostic probes labelled transparently; resource-depth indicator clarified; maintenance/status notes added.
  • v29: repaired mobile small-step formatting and animation controls/stacking.

  • v27: resource-link audit and blue/grey background restored.

Statutory objectives are kept as separate cards across all primary strands. Expand a card for progression, teaching points, misconceptions, representations, assessment checks and curated objective-specific resources. Broad source pages stay at strand level; objective cards only surface close mathematical matches.

Representation journeys

See how representations deliberately change as mathematical thinking becomes more sophisticated. The aim is not to use every representation, but to know what each one makes visible and when it should give way to a more efficient model.

What changes by year?

Choose a concept to see how the mathematical demand, representations, language and typical misconceptions develop from EYFS to Year 6.

Whole-school maths language & methods

A shared reference for the mathematical language, method conventions and representation principles used across the school and in the Parent Maths Guide.

Purpose: consistency does not mean every calculation must look identical or that pupils use one method. It means that when the same mathematical idea appears in different year groups, adults use compatible language and explain the structure in the same way. The parent wording below is intentionally simpler, but preserves the same mathematics.

Year group overview

See the full statutory picture for one year, then jump straight into any objective for teaching guidance and planning support.

Interactive maths tools

Purpose-built manipulatives and teaching tools aligned to the Navigator’s representation and calculation principles. Use Teach to model, Explore for pupil manipulation and discussion, and Challenge for prediction and reasoning. Tools open in a new tab and can also be embedded individually in Google Sites.

Misconceptions index

Every "common misconception / watch-for" already recorded against a statutory objective, gathered in one place and grouped by strand. Nothing here is new: it is the same wording that appears on each objective card. Use it to plan what to watch for across a unit, then follow a link to the objective it belongs to.
